title: Get started
text: Now simulated data, can fit SEM using INLAvaan. model syntax similar lavaan, making easy specify model. details model syntax, refer lavaan website. INLAvaan provides mirror functions main model fitting functions lavaan: acfa() mirrors lavaan::cfa() confirmatory factor analysis; asem() mirrors lavaan::sem() structural equation models; agrowth() mirrors lavaan::growth() latent growth curve models. code fit SEM model : lavaan::sem(), model fitted without mean structure default (meanstructure = FALSE). Rather profiling means lavaan , INLAvaan assigns saturated means flat priors marginalises analytically, keeps likelihood proper Bayesian object. Intercepts can instead modelled explicitly meanstructure = TRUE. See mean structures article two treatments relate model comparisons across meaningful. INLAvaan computes approximation posterior density way Laplace approximation (Tierney et al. 1989; Jamil Rue 2026a). joint mode Hessian needs computed, gives Gaussian distribution joint posterior parameters. default method optimisation stats::nlminb(), optimisers can used specifying optim_method = "ucminf" ucminf package optim_method = "optim" call stats::optim() function method "BFGS". , marginal posterior distributions parameter can obtained one several ways, including 1) Skew normal fitting (marginal_method = "skewnorm", default method, see Chiuchiolo et al. 2023); 2) Two-piece asymmetric Gaussian fitting (marginal_method = "asymgaus", see Martins et al. 2013); 3) Direct marginalisation joint Gaussian posterior (marginal_method = "marggaus"); 4) Sampling joint Gaussian posterior (marginal_method = "sampling"). marginal posterior distributions obtained, can use compute derived quantities interest via copula sampling. posterior predictive p-values (Gelman et al. 1996) Deviance Information Criterion (DIC, Spiegelhalter et al. 2002) computed way. test argument names post-estimation quantities compute: default test = "standard" computes PPP DIC, test = "full" adds leave-one-cross-validation WAIC results (see model comparison section ) stores fit, test = "none" skips . Often, posterior sampling takes longer model fitting , number samples can controlled via nsamp argument (default nsamp = 1000).

title: Bayesian Fit Indices
text: Classical SEM fit indices (RMSEA, CFI, TLI, etc.) computed single maximum-likelihood chi-square statistic. Bayesian SEM, parameters random, posterior draw yields different chi-square value , therefore, different set fit indices. INLAvaan provides Bayesian analogues common indices, following framework Garnier-Villarreal Jorgensen (2020) (implemented blavaan). vignette covers: Mathematical definitions Bayesian fit indices. two rescaling methods ("devM" "MCMC"). worked example Holzinger–Swineford data. Comparison baseline model (incremental indices). Differences INLAvaan blavaan.

title: Bayesian Fit Indices
text: Let \(\boldsymbol\theta^{(s)}\) denote \(s\)-th posterior draw model parameters (\(s = 1, \dots, S\)). per-sample deviance chi-square \[   \chi^2_s = 2 \bigl[\ell_{\text{sat}} - \ell(\boldsymbol\theta^{(s)})\bigr], \] \(\ell_{\text{sat}}\) log-likelihood saturated model (sample moments equal model moments) \(\ell(\boldsymbol\theta^{(s)})\) log-likelihood evaluated \(s\)-th draw. equals \(N \, F_{\text{ML}}(\boldsymbol\theta^{(s)})\), \(F_{\text{ML}}\) ML discrepancy function. INLAvaan supports two rescaling methods, controlled rescale argument: "devM" (default). Uses DIC-based effective number parameters \(p_D\). \[   d_s = \chi^2_s - p_D, \qquad   \mathrm{df} = p - p_D, \qquad   N_{\mathrm{adj}} = N. \] \(p_D\) unreasonable (\(p_D \leq 0\) \(p_D \geq p\)), INLAvaan falls back using \(p_D = q\) (number free parameters). "MCMC". Uses classical chi-square \(N - 1\) scaling. \[   d_s = \frac{N - 1}{N} \chi^2_s, \qquad   \mathrm{df} = p - q, \qquad   N_{\mathrm{adj}} = N - G, \] \(q\) number free parameters \(G\) number groups. cases per-sample noncentrality parameter \(\hat\lambda_s = \max(d_s - \mathrm{df},\, 0)\). following indices computed posterior draw \(s\), generating posterior distribution. BRMSEA (Bayesian RMSEA). \[   \text{BRMSEA}_s = \sqrt{\frac{\hat\lambda_s}{\mathrm{df} \cdot N_\text{adj}}} \cdot \sqrt{G}. \] BGammaHat. \[   \text{BGammaHat}_s = \frac{v}{v + 2\hat\lambda_s / N_\text{adj}}, \] \(v = \sum_g p_g\) total number observed variables across groups. Adjusted BGammaHat. \[   \text{adjBGammaHat}_s = 1 - \frac{p}{\mathrm{df}} \bigl(1 - \text{BGammaHat}_s\bigr). \] BMc (McDonald’s centrality index). \[   \text{BMc}_s = \exp\!\bigl(-\tfrac{1}{2}\hat\lambda_s / N_\text{adj}\bigr). \] Incremental indices compare target model baseline (null) model. Let \(d_s^{(0)}\), \(\mathrm{df}^{(0)}\), \(\hat\lambda_s^{(0)}\) denote corresponding quantities baseline model. BCFI (Bayesian CFI). \[   \text{BCFI}_s = 1 - \frac{\hat\lambda_s}{\hat\lambda_s^{(0)}}. \] BTLI (Bayesian TLI). \[   \text{BTLI}_s = \frac{d_s^{(0)} / \mathrm{df}^{(0)} - d_s / \mathrm{df}}{d_s^{(0)} / \mathrm{df}^{(0)} - 1}. \] BNFI (Bayesian NFI). \[   \text{BNFI}_s = \frac{d_s^{(0)} - d_s}{d_s^{(0)}}. \] posterior expectations (EAP), standard deviations, quantile-based credible intervals, modes distributions reported summary() method.

title: Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation
text: well model predict new data? Leave-one-(LOO) cross-validation answers holding one unit time, refitting model remaining data, scoring held-unit refitted posterior. total score expected log predictive density, \[   \mathrm{elpd}_{\mathrm{loo}} = \sum_{u=1}^n \log p(y_u \mid y_{-u}), \] rewards models predict well automatically penalises overfitting, making natural criterion comparing models. Computed naively, LOO needs \(n\) refits. MCMC-based packages blavaan avoid importance-sampling posterior draws (Vehtari et al. 2017), still requires full set MCMC draws. INLAvaan instead exploits Laplace machinery: loo() approximates case-deletion posterior Taylor expansion around full-data posterior summary, entire LOO computed single fit, refitting sampling. Two unit types scored, resolved automatically model: LOSO (leave-one-subject-): single-level models, one unit per row. LOCO (leave-one-cluster-): two-level models, one unit per cluster – relevant predictive question “well model predict new cluster?”.

title: Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation
text: loo() computes everything fit’s Laplace summary \(\mathcal{N}(\theta^*, \Omega)\). exact identity turns held-predictive density expectation full-data posterior, evaluated closed form Taylor-expanding unit’s log-likelihood \(\ell_u(\theta) = \log p(y_u \mid \theta)\) \(\theta^*\). \(s_u\) \(H_u\) gradient Hessian \(\ell_u\) , two orders \[ \begin{aligned}   \log \mathrm{CPO}_u^{(1)} &= \ell_u - \tfrac12 s_u^\top \Omega\, s_u, \\   \log \mathrm{CPO}_u^{(2)} &= \ell_u     - \tfrac12 s_u^\top (\Omega^{-1} + H_u)^{-1} s_u     + \tfrac12 \log \lvert + \Omega H_u \rvert , \end{aligned} \] second order additionally handing back information unit lent posterior. headline elpd_loo sum second-order terms, standard error \(\sqrt{n \, \widehat{\mathrm{var}}(\log \mathrm{CPO}_u)}\); looic \(= -2\,\mathrm{elpd}_{\mathrm{loo}}\), p_loo (loo package’s effective number parameters, matching loo::loo()) comes analogous expansion pointwise predictive density. Two checks, free result, tell whether trust expansion. first existence condition enforced automatically: \(\log \mathrm{CPO}_u^{(2)}\) exists exactly \(\Omega^{-1} + H_u \succ 0\), equivalently unit’s leverage k_max (largest eigenvalue \(-\Omega H_u\), reported per_unit) stays 1. unit 1 carries much curvature whole posterior direction, true LOO term genuinely extreme. cases, whole result reverts first order, warning naming units inspect. second gap check, printed every second-order result. first- second-order totals settled expansion differ \(p_D/2\), approached , printout reports gap, reference \(p_D/2\) (pd_trace, trace form \(\operatorname{tr}(-\Omega \sum_u H_u)\)), excess one . large positive excess says expansion settled sample. threshold applied, reading left user, validation gap always within elpd units zero well-behaved models.

title: Multilevel SEM
text: INLAvaan (following lavaan syntax), specify model level using level: <block> keywords. example, Level 1: define latent variable fw (Student Ability) regress individual predictors (x). Level 2: define latent variable fb (School Quality) regress school-level predictors (w). use asem() function (Approximate SEM) fit model. Crucially, must specify cluster argument identify grouping variable.
code: mod <- "   level: 1       # Measurement model (Within-student)       fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3       # Structural model: Individual predictors       fw ~ x1 + x2 + x3    level: 2       # Measurement model (Between-school)       fb =~ y1 + y2 + y3       # Structural model: School-level predictors       fb ~ w1 + w2 " fit <- asem(mod, data = Demo.twolevel, cluster = "cluster") #> ℹ Mode finding and Hessian computation. #> ✔ Posterior mode and Hessian. title: Sampling from the Generative Model
text: Let \(\boldsymbol\theta^{(s)}\) (\(s = 1, \dots, S\)) denote one parameter draw. draw SEM matrices \(\boldsymbol\Lambda\), \(\boldsymbol\Psi\), \(\mathbf{B}\), \(\boldsymbol\alpha\), \(\boldsymbol\nu\), \(\boldsymbol\Theta\) constructed. generative chain : 1. Latent variables. \[ \boldsymbol\eta^{(s)} \sim \mathcal{N}\!\bigl(   (\mathbf{} - \mathbf{B})^{-1}\boldsymbol\alpha,\;   \boldsymbol\Phi \bigr), \qquad \boldsymbol\Phi = (\mathbf{} - \mathbf{B})^{-1}\boldsymbol\Psi\,   [(\mathbf{} - \mathbf{B})^{-1}]'. \] 2. Observed variables. \[ \mathbf{y}^{*(s)} \sim \mathcal{N}\!\bigl(   \boldsymbol\Lambda\,\boldsymbol\eta^{(s)} + \boldsymbol\nu,\;   \boldsymbol\Theta \bigr). \] prior = FALSE (default), \(\boldsymbol\theta^{(s)}\) comes posterior; prior = TRUE, parameter drawn independently prior.

title: Sampling from the Generative Model

what: Comparing samples to the fitted marginals
title: Sampling from the Generative Model
text: INLAvaan approximates marginal posterior skew-normal density. can overlay sampling() histogram (drawn via copula method) top fitted density curve stored pdf_data verify agree. Figure 1: Copula samples (histogram) versus fitted skew-normal marginal (red curve) free parameters.
code: # 1. Draw copula samples samp_cop <- sampling(fit, type = "lavaan", nsamp = 1000, samp_copula = TRUE)  # 2. Retrieve the fitted skew-normal densities int <- fit@external$inlavaan_internal pdf_data <- int$pdf_data  # 3. Build a long data frame for ggplot par_names <- colnames(samp_cop) hist_df <- data.frame(   param = rep(par_names, each = nrow(samp_cop)),   value = as.vector(samp_cop) ) hist_df$param <- factor(hist_df$param, levels = par_names)  curve_df <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(nm, df) {   data.frame(param = nm, x = df$x, y = df$y) }, par_names, pdf_data[par_names])) curve_df$param <- factor(curve_df$param, levels = par_names)  # 4. Plot ggplot(hist_df, aes(x = value)) +   geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50,                  fill = "grey40", alpha = 0.5) +   geom_line(data = curve_df, aes(x = x, y = y),             colour = "#00A6AA", linewidth = 0.8) +   facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free") +   labs(x = "Parameter value", y = "Density",        title = "Copula samples vs. fitted skew-normal posterior") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

title: Sampling from the Generative Model
text: default, sampling() uses copula method, respects skew-normal marginals. Setting samp_copula = FALSE uses multivariate Gaussian (Laplace) approximation instead. difference visible parameters asymmetric posteriors, variance components. Figure 2: Comparison marginal histograms copula sampling (blue) Gaussian sampling (orange) parameters. symmetric posteriors (e.g., factor loadings), two methods nearly identical. positively-skewed posteriors (e.g., residual variances), copula method captures asymmetry Gaussian approximation symmetric construction.
code: samp_gauss <- sampling(fit, type = "lavaan", nsamp = 5000, samp_copula = FALSE)  cop_df <- data.frame(   param = rep(par_names, each = nrow(samp_cop)),   value = as.vector(samp_cop),   method = "Copula" ) gauss_df <- data.frame(   param = rep(par_names, each = nrow(samp_gauss)),   value = as.vector(samp_gauss),   method = "Gaussian" ) both_df <- rbind(cop_df, gauss_df) both_df$param <- factor(both_df$param, levels = par_names) both_df$method <- factor(both_df$method, levels = c("Copula", "Gaussian"))  ggplot(both_df, aes(x = value, fill = method)) +   geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 50,                  alpha = 0.45, position = "identity") +   facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free") +   scale_fill_manual(values = c(Copula = "#00A6AA", Gaussian = "#F18F00")) +   labs(x = "Parameter value", y = "Density", fill = "Method",        title = "Copula vs. Gaussian posterior sampling") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +   theme(legend.position = "top")

title: Approximate Bayesian Latent Variable Analysis
text: Efficient approximate Bayesian inference Structural Equation Models. Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods remain gold standard exact Bayesian inference, can prohibitively slow iterative model development. INLAvaan offers rapid alternative latent variable analysis, delivering Bayesian results (near) speed frequentist estimators. achieves custom, ground-implementation Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA), engineered specifically lavaan modelling framework.

title: Approximate Bayesian Latent Variable Analysis

title: INLAvaan: Approximate Bayesian Latent Variable Analysis — INLAvaan-package
text: Implements approximate Bayesian inference Structural Equation Models (SEM) using custom adaptation Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (Rue et al., 2009) doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x  described Jamil Rue (2026a) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2603.25690 . Provides computationally efficient alternative Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) Bayesian estimation, allowing users fit latent variable models using 'lavaan' syntax. See also companion paper implementation workflows, Jamil Rue (2026b) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2604.00671 .

text: \(\bar{D}\) \(\hat{D}\) two ingredients Deviance Information Criterion, \(DIC = \bar{D} + p_D\) \(p_D = \bar{D} - \hat{D}\) effective number parameters. Use compare() compare models DIC (Bayes factors, LOO/WAIC) rather comparing raw deviances directly. \(p_D\) estimated posterior draws. loo() reaches quantity closed form pd_trace, trace \(\mathrm{tr}(\Sigma \mathcal{})\); two routes estimate one target agree exactly finite sample. code: # Fit a SN curve to gamma log-density logdens <- function(x) dgamma(x, shape = 3, rate = 1, log = TRUE)  x_grid <- seq(0.1, 8, length.out = 21) y_log  <- sapply(x_grid, logdens) y_log  <- y_log - max(y_log)  # normalise to have maximum at zero  res <- fit_skew_normal(x_grid, y_log, temp = 10) unlist(res) #>           xi        omega        alpha         logC            k         rmse  #>  0.842445393  2.539226101  3.310505376  1.332422700 10.000000000  0.002109188  #>         nmad  #>  0.173298470   # Compare truth vs skew-normal approximation x_fine <- seq(0.1, 8, length.out = 200) y_true <- exp(logdens(x_fine)) y_sn   <- dsnorm(x_fine, xi = res$xi, omega = res$omega, alpha = res$alpha)  plot(x_fine, y_true, type = "n", xlab = "x", ylab = "Density", bty = "n") polygon(c(x_fine, rev(x_fine)), c(y_true, rep(0, length(x_fine))),         col = adjustcolor("#131516", 0.25), border = NA) lines(x_fine, y_sn, col = "#00A6AA", lwd = 2) legend("topright", legend = c("Truth", "SN Approx."),        fill = c(adjustcolor("#131516", 0.25), NA), border = NA,        col = c(NA, "#00A6AA"), lwd = c(NA, 2), lty = c(NA, 1),        bty = "n")

title: Log-Likelihood for INLAvaan Models — logLik
text: marginal log-likelihood already integrates (Laplace- approximated) posterior, scale classical log-likelihood passed AIC()/BIC() – double-penalise model complexity evidence already accounted . Use compare() compare models via Bayes factors, DIC, LOO/WAIC. plug-variant exists users specifically want point-estimate-based classical comparison. AIC()/BIC() INLAvaan fit disabled (mirroring anova()): large-sample asymptotic approximations quantities INLAvaan already computes directly – AIC approximates predictive accuracy, loo()/waic() already estimate rigorously; BIC approximates \(-2\) times log marginal likelihood, logLik() already returns directly (Laplace approximation). Point-estimate AIC/BIC remain available reporting-convention purposes via AIC(logLik(object, type = "plugin")) / BIC(logLik(object, type = "plugin")).

title: Approximate Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation for INLAvaan Models — loo
text: Computes leave-one-(LOO) cross-validation fitted INLAvaan model single fit, refitting sampling, via Taylor approximation case-deletion posterior around Laplace summary. Single-level models scored per subject (leave-one-subject-, LOSO); two-level models scored per cluster (leave-one-cluster-, LOCO).

title: Fast Approximation of Skew-Normal Quantile Function — qsnorm_fast
text: function implements high-performance approximation skew-normal quantile function based algorithm described Luu (2016). method uses domain decomposition strategy achieve high accuracy (\(< 10^{-7}\) relative error) without iterative numerical inversion. domain split two regions: Tail Regions: extreme probabilities \(\vert u \vert\) large, quantile approximated using Lambert W-function, \(W(z)\), solving \(z = \Phi(q)\) via asymptotic expansion: $$q \approx \sqrt{2 W\left(\frac{1}{2\pi (1-p)^2}\right)}$$ Central Region: main body distribution, function uses high-order Taylor expansion inverse error function around carefully selected expansion point $x_0$: $$\Phi^{-1}(p) \approx \sum_{k=0}^5 c_k (z - x_0)^k$$ approach significantly faster standard numerical inversion (e.g., uniroot) maintaining sufficient precision statistical applications.

title: Fast Approximation of Skew-Normal Quantile Function — qsnorm_fast
text: Luu, T. (2016). Fast accurate parallel computation quantile functions random number generation (Doctoral thesis). UCL (University College London). https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1482128/

title: Widely Applicable Information Criterion for INLAvaan Models — waic
text: Writing \(\ell_u(\theta) = \log p(y_u \mid \theta)\) expanding second order posterior mode, posterior taken \(N(\theta^*, \Omega)\), WAIC terms available closed form: pointwise log predictive density \(\mathrm{lpd}_u\) Gaussian integral loo() computes, penalty polynomial $$p_{\mathrm{waic},u} = \mathrm{Var}[\ell_u(\theta)]   = s_u^\top \Omega\, s_u   + \tfrac12 \mathrm{tr}\!\left[(H_u \Omega)^2\right],$$ \(s_u\) \(H_u\) unit's score Hessian. \(\mathrm{elpd}_{\mathrm{waic}} = \sum_u (\mathrm{lpd}_u - p_{\mathrm{waic},u})\) \(\mathrm{WAIC} = -2\, \mathrm{elpd}_{\mathrm{waic}}\). Existence. \(p_{\mathrm{waic},u}\) polynomial posterior moments, unlike lpd log CPO integrals loo() finite every unit carries condition . second-order WAIC therefore exists exactly lpd term : \(\Omega^{-1} - H_u\) positive definite, equivalently \(k_{\min} > -1\) spectrum \(k\) \(-\Omega H_u\). log CPO condition \(k_{\max} < 1\) irrelevant , since WAIC reads case-deletion term: unit whose deleted posterior improper can still carry exact second-order WAIC. lpd term fails, every estimate reported first order units warns – \(\mathrm{elpd}_{\mathrm{waic}}\) headline predictive score, mixing two Taylor orders within one reported number exactly loo() refuses \(\mathrm{elpd}_{\mathrm{loo}}\) (mixed alternative reserved p_loo, secondary diagnostic). fallback exact rather merely lower-order: identity \(\mathrm{lpd}^{(1)}_u - p^{(1)}_{\mathrm{waic},u} = \log \mathrm{CPO}^{(1)}_u\) holds pointwise, first-order WAIC first-order LOO score. threshold applied: loo(), existence condition package acts . model restrictions loo() apply, flavour rule: fits fixed.x = TRUE scored conditionally exogenous covariates, fits fixed.x = FALSE jointly (see loo()). composites, \(p_{\mathrm{waic}}\) also counts indicator (co)variances lavaan fixes sample values, p_loo . Marginal vs conditional WAIC (two-level models). default per-cluster scoring marginal WAIC, corresponds leave-one-cluster-cross-validation – prediction new cluster. Setting type = "loso" scores conditional WAIC, corresponding leave-one-unit-– prediction new observation within observed cluster. two answer different questions easily conflated (Merkle, Furr & Rabe-Hesketh, 2019); per-cluster marginal usual model-comparison target, default, type = "loso" warns. matches loo(type = "loso") – two read estimand expansion. inlavaan()'s test includes "loo" "waic" (e.g. test = "full"), WAIC derived fit time Taylor pass LOO extra cost stored fit: waic(fit) returns stored result called default arguments, fitmeasures() reports waic, p_waic, se_waic part "" free. default test = "standard" nothing stored waic(fit) computes demand. loo package attached masks generic, dispatch INLAvaan objects continues work.

Requesting meanstructure = FALSE two-level model now warns fits meanstructure = TRUE (mean structure required ). conditional (fixed.x = TRUE) flavour — default SEM exogenous covariates — fully supported: mean marginalisation factorises blockwise, unit scored difference two exchangeable conditionals, frozen-covariate term entering exact constant. predict() now centres conditioning data model-implied means (saturated sample means model mean structure) drawing factor scores predicted observed variables. Previously kernels conditioned raw data, offsetting every factor score constant grows variable means. sampling() simulate() draws observed variables models without mean structure now include saturated (sample) means, posterior predictive replicates live data scale instead centred zero. sampling() simulate() longer error models single latent variable, saturated-mean recovery now robust missing data (replicate columns previously NA missing = "pairwise"). PPP’s observed discrepancy now uses unbiased (divisor n-1) sample covariance, matching scale Wishart-replicated covariances compared ; previously divisor-n form made PPP slightly optimistic (O(1/n) effect, models). coef() (merged parameter table, fitted values, implied moments) now reports covariance parameters covariance scale.
